questions.question: Why were specialized neural network architectures like CNNs and RNNs needed?
options: Standard neural networks cannot perform any calculations
Standard networks are too simple for large, complex data like images and long text
Standard networks only work on tiny datasets
Standard networks can only classify numbers

questions.question: A CNN is most suitable for which kind of data?
In CNNs, the mathematical operation used to scan an image with a small window is called:
The filter or kernel in a CNN is best described as:
options: A tiny grid of numbers that slides over the image
A layer that only stores labels

questions.question: What does a high convolution score usually indicate?
options: The filter found an important pattern like an edge or curve
The image has no useful information

questions.question: Pooling in a CNN mainly helps by:
options: Keeping only the most important values and reducing data
Adding more pixels to the image

questions.question: Which sequence best describes how CNNs build higher-level vision understanding?
options: Convolution and pooling stacked in layers

questions.question: Why are CNNs poor at understanding sentences compared with RNNs?
options: CNNs are designed for images, not sequential order
CNNs only work on audio files

questions.question: A sequence is best defined as:
What special feature allows an RNN to remember previous information?
options: A loop that passes memory forward

questions.question: The vanishing gradient problem occurs when:
options: The learning rate becomes very large
Repeated multiplication of small values makes gradients nearly zero
The model has too many filters

questions.question: Why does vanishing gradient hurt RNN learning on long sequences?
options: It prevents the model from storing any output
It weakens learning from earlier parts of the sequence
It increases the number of filters

questions.question: Which architecture was created to fix the vanishing gradient problem in RNNs?
An LSTM is best described as an RNN with:
What is the role of the LSTM cell state?
options: To carry important memories through long sequences
To delete all old information instantly

questions.question: The gates in an LSTM mainly help the network to:
options: Choose what to forget and what to keep

questions.question: The conveyor belt analogy for LSTM's cell state emphasizes its ability to:
options: Carry memory safely across a long sequence

questions.question: Which task was LSTM especially valuable for before newer models became dominant?
Why did LSTMs become the gold standard for many language tasks for years?
options: They could preserve important memory over long data
They used fewer pixels than CNNs
They worked only on small texts

questions.question: Which pairing is correctly matched?
options: LSTM — improved long-term memory in sequences
Pooling — storing important words in text
